knowledge:
- key_parameters: eset=The ExpressionSet object containing expression data and phenoData ;; annotation=The annotation package (e.g., hgu95av2.db) used by annotateEset to map probe IDs to Entrez IDs, Symbols, and Gene Names ;; df=A data frame (typically from topTable) containing differential expression results ;; grp.factor=A factor defining the experimental groups for plotting in makeImages ;; collist=A list of column indices from the contrast matrix to compare in makeVenn ;; .modifyDF / .mofifyDF=A list of functions (like entrezLinks, affyLinks) passed to publish to turn IDs into clickable HTML hyperlinks
- alternatives: ReportingTools default publishing=Mentioned as generating a combination of dotplot and boxplot by default, which the author finds "weird"; affycoretools::makeImages is preferred for cleaner dotplots/boxplots with links to larger plots ;; xtable or knitr::kable=Mentioned as alternatives for generating summary tables of comparisons with links to individual HTML reports
- when_to_use: Use when performing standard microarray or RNA-Seq differential expression analysis (typically with limma) and there is a need to generate reproducible, user-friendly, and interactive HTML reports for collaborators or clients.
- pitfalls: Typographical errors in arguments in the documentation (e.g., .mofifyDF is used in one code block and .modifyDF in another) ;; Generating many individual plot files can clutter the working directory; users should use the default "reports" subdirectory to keep files organized ;; Ensure the feature names of the ExpressionSet do not contain characters like "/" which might break file paths (the docs show featureNames(eset) <- gsub("/", "_", featureNames(eset)) in an unprinted block)

workflows.name: differential_expression_and_html_reporting
workflows.intent: Annotate expression data, fit a linear model, generate gene-level plots, and compile results into an interactive HTML report with clickable links.
input: eset (ExpressionSet containing expression data and phenoData)
workflows.stages: 1. Annotate the ExpressionSet using annotateEset ;; 2. Fit a linear model and compute contrasts using limma ;; 3. Generate gene-level plots for top differentially expressed genes using makeImages ;; 4. Publish the results to an HTML report with clickable gene links using ReportingTools and finish
workflows.code:
eset <- annotateEset(eset, hgu95av2.db)
fit <- lmFit(eset, design)
fit2 <- contrasts.fit(fit, contrast)
fit2 <- eBayes(fit)
d.f <- topTable(fit2, 2)
out <- makeImages(df = d.f, eset = eset, grp.factor = pd$type, design = design,
                  contrast = contrast, colind = 1, repdir = ".")
htab <- HTMLReport("afile3", "My cool results, affycoretools style")
publish(out$df, htab, .mofifyDF = list(entrezLinks, affyLinks))
finish(htab)

workflows.name: interactive_venn_diagram_generation
workflows.intent: Generate an interactive Venn diagram showing overlapping significant genes between multiple comparisons.
input: fit2 (MArrayLM object from limma after eBayes)
workflows.stages: 1. Define the list of contrast columns to compare ;; 2. Create the Venn object using makeVenn ;; 3. Generate and display the Venn diagram with captions using vennInLine
workflows.code:
collist <- list(1:2)
venn <- makeVenn(fit2, contrast, design, collist = collist, adj.meth = "none")
cap <- list(paste("A Venn diagram. Note that the first sentence is bolded",
                  "and blue, whereas the rest is normal type and black. Usually",
                  "one would use a more useful caption than this one."))
vennInLine(venn, cap)
